title: Vanishing Gradient
summary: In deep networks, backpropagated gradients shrink exponentially layer-by-layer, leaving early layers with virtually zero parameter updates.
problem: In deep feedforward networks, during backpropagation, gradients are multiplied by small weights/derivatives layer-by-layer. As depth increases, the gradient shrinks exponentially, leaving early layers with virtually zero updates.
intuition: Signals decay by a factor < 1 at each layer. By the time backpropagation reaches layer 0, the derivative signal has attenuated into numerical insignificance.
analogy: Passing a whisper down a line of 50 people — by the time it reaches the first person, the original message is completely lost.
visualExplanation: Gradient particles decrease in size, transparency, and speed as they propagate backward from output to input layers.

mathematics.description: Chain rule multiplication of layer Jacobians. When derivative values are strictly smaller than 1, repeated multiplication over L layers causes exponential decay: \mathcal{O}(\gamma^L) \to 0.

variables.\\sigma'(z_i): Derivative of activation function at layer i

causes: Small weight initializations causing magnitude reduction at each layer
symptoms: Early layer weights remain unchanged during training
Training loss plateaus early despite high capacity
solutions: Use ReLU, LeakyReLU, or GELU activations

references.author: Sepp Hochreiter

title: Exploding Gradient
summary: If weights are initialized too large or gradients unclipped, derivative products explode exponentially, creating numerical overflow and training instability.
problem: If weights are initialized too large (or gradients are scaled poorly), backpropagated derivatives are repeatedly multiplied by factors > 1, growing exponentially.
intuition: The gradients balloon to infinity (NaN), causing the network weights to oscillate wildly and completely destabilize learning.
analogy: An audio feedback loop where a microphone picks up its own speaker output, causing the volume to scream louder and louder until clipping.
visualExplanation: Gradient particles balloon rapidly in size, violently shaking nodes, turning bright crimson red, and causing chaotic trajectory spikes.

mathematics.description: Repeated matrix multiplication with eigenvalues greater than 1 results in exponential growth: \mathcal{O}(\lambda^L) \to \infty.

variables.W_i: Weight matrix at layer i with spectral radius > 1

causes: Unclipped learning rates or step sizes
symptoms: Loss rapidly becomes NaN or Infinity
Weights oscillate wildly between extreme positive and negative values

references.title: On the difficulty of training Recurrent Neural Networks
references.author: Razvan Pascanu, Tomas Mikolov, Yoshua Bengio

title: Residual Connections (ResNet)
summary: Identity skip connections bypass weight paths, allowing gradient derivatives to flow backwards directly through constant addition.
problem: Standard deep networks suffer from optimization degradation. Skip connections bypass the weights, allowing gradients to flow backwards directly.
intuition: Identity skip connections act as gradient superhighways. Even if weights inside the main path vanish, the gradient flows unimpeded through the shortcut path (+ 1 term in derivative).
analogy: An express highway bypass alongside local city streets. Drivers can skip traffic lights and travel across the city without stopping.
visualExplanation: Green particles travel smoothly across curved arc bypass lines directly between non-adjacent layers, keeping backpropagation alive.

mathematics.formula: H(x) = F(x) + x \implies \frac{\partial H}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial F}{\partial x} + 1
mathematics.description: Adding the identity term guarantees that the Jacobian matrix derivative has an additive constant term of 1.0, preserving gradient magnitude.

causes: Optimization degradation in ultra-deep networks (50+ layers)
symptoms: Deeper networks having higher training error than shallow counterparts
solutions: Identity mapping skip connections F(x) + x

references.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
references.author: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun

title: Dense Connections (DenseNet)
summary: Every layer connects directly to all subsequent layers in a block, establishing direct multi-channel gradient propagation paths.
problem: Traditional residual additions merge features together, diluting distinct layer representations. Concatenation keeps features separate and directly accessible.
intuition: Every layer is connected directly to every other layer in a block. Grad signals flow backwards from the output to every single intermediate layer via multiple parallel channels.
analogy: A conference room where every single participant has a direct private telephone link to all other participants rather than passing notes down a row.
visualExplanation: Multiple purple bezier arc pathways transmit gradient particles simultaneously from the output layer to all preceding hidden layers.

mathematics.description: Feature maps from all preceding layers are concatenated along the channel dimension, giving direct derivative access to all earlier representations.

variables.x_l: Output feature maps at layer l

causes: Feature dilution and bottlenecking in standard sequential networks
symptoms: In-efficient parameter usage and redundant feature learning

references.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
references.author: Gao Huang, Zhuang Liu, Laurens van der Maaten, Kilian Q. Weinberger

title: Batch Normalization
summary: Normalizes layer input distributions across mini-batches to zero mean and unit variance, preventing internal covariate shift and stabilizing backprop.
problem: As weights update, the distribution of inputs to internal layers shifts constantly (Internal Covariate Shift), forcing subsequent layers to continuously adapt to changing scales.
intuition: Calculates the mean and variance of activations across a mini-batch, normalizing them to zero mean and unit variance before scaling/shifting them with learnable parameters.
analogy: Standardizing test scores to a zero-mean bell curve before grading so that easy or hard exams maintain consistent grading scales.
visualExplanation: Cyan normalization barriers at each layer resettle and equalize gradient particle size, speed, and alpha to healthy baseline levels.

mathematics.description: Subtract mini-batch mean, divide by standard deviation, and apply learnable scale gamma and shift beta parameters.

causes: Internal Covariate Shift during gradient updates
symptoms: Necessity for extremely small learning rates
solutions: Insert Batch Normalization layers prior to activation functions

references.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
references.author: Sergey Ioffe, Christian Szegedy
